correctness.rationale: There are precisely 24 strict rankings per agent and 24 priorities. Complete exact integer enumeration of all 331,776 labeled four-agent/three-object preference profiles gives waste-numerator histogram (317664,1728,5040,6912,432), no numerator above four, exactly 432 extremizers in six disjoint agent/object relabeling orbits of size 72, and one maximizing acceptable pair per extremizer. The full-domain C++ implementation checks normal forms, symmetry-orbit coverage, and witness uniqueness. A separately written available-list Python simulator checks a justified sixfold object-label quotient of 55,296 profiles, independently reproduces every count, and verifies common 24-priority allocation vectors and marginals. All tests executed successfully. The finite domain is complete, not sampled; no infinite generalization is claimed.

originality.rationale: Basteck and Ehlers (2026), Section 3, Lemma 1 and Appendix B establish the sharp 1/6 waste bound and exhibit an equality example. The inspected primary argument does not enumerate all equality profiles or prove the six-orbit normal form, unique maximizing pair, frequency 1/768, full waste histogram, or priority-by-priority invariance. Searches and relevant record comparisons uncovered no equivalent coverage. The result is a full equality-case classification for the minimally nontrivial natural market, not a new proof of the known bound. Unindexed prior work remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed finite classification, perhaps under different terminology, could contain the exact equality orbits or histogram; failure to find it is not a proof of priority.
The complete text of the older Martini (2016) paper was not inspected, although the more directly matching Basteck–Ehlers 2026 primary paper was materially read.
The theorem is confined to four agents and three objects; it does not establish a dimension-independent structural law.

value.rationale: The equality cases for the sharp known one-sixth marginal waste bound are a motivated, mathematically natural target in the first nontrivial 4-by-3 outside-option market. The exact six orbit normal forms, one unique triggering pair, full integer histogram, common per-priority outcome equivalence and rare 1/768 impartial-culture incidence sharpen the worst-case result substantively. These characterize when the upper bound is tight and which additional acceptable choices are behaviorally inert, rather than recomputing the bound, changing notation, or choosing an arbitrary subfamily.
